reasons: Lake identity record matches State v. Weaver, Tex. Crim. App., decided 2011-09-28, docket PD-1635-10.
Lake citations include official display 2011 Tex. Crim. App. LEXIS 1320, parallel 349 S.W.3d 521, and vendor-neutral 2011 WL 4715178.
residual_risks: No Lens A defect; citation hierarchy/currency beyond the disclosed lake selection is not independently checked.

defect.evidence_quote: The record, viewed in the light most favorable to the trial judge’s ruling, supports an implicit fact finding that the van was parked in a protected, non-public area of the business premises rather than in a parking lot open to the public.
defect.problem: The disclosed opinion supports a non-public business-premises / scope-of-consent holding, not a curtilage holding, and does not justify labeling Weaver as a Key Curtilage case.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove the Key Curtilage home role, or downgrade to a related/illustrative cross-reference that expressly says the case concerns protected non-public commercial premises rather than residential curtilage.

reasons: The opinion frames the protected area as a welding shop, workshop bay/loading dock, and non-public business premises.
The cached text contains no curtilage terminology or residential-curtilage analysis.
residual_risks: There may be an external taxonomy reason to place private commercial premises on a Curtilage page, but that taxonomy is not disclosed here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use a narrower label such as Consent Searches, Business Premises, or Dog Sniffs unless the Curtilage page explicitly includes commercial-premises analogues.

reasons: The text states that officers needed permission to be where they initiated the dog sniff and did not have it.
The opinion says the Caballes/Place dog-sniff rule is premised on the officer and dog having a right to stand where the sniff occurs.
The court held the officers had completed the Bear search, lingered beyond the scope of consent, brought in the dog without authorization, and suppression was affirmed.
residual_risks: The holding is fact-bound and close-call; it should not be generalized to public parking lots, open-to-public business areas, or situations with independent legal authorization.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add that Weaver had also unequivocally refused consent to search the van before the dog was deployed.

reasons: Lens A does not assess treatment or currency.
The treatment fields in the assertion mirror the lake treatment stub: field_i_validity unverified, null as-of fields, composite_basis unverified, varies_by_point false, and the same scope note.
residual_risks: Treatment/good-law accuracy is reserved for Lens B.

reasons: Lens A does not raise treatment-weight findings.
The disclosed record identifies the court as Tex. Crim. App. and court_level as state, which is consistent with a state persuasive label in this federal corpus.
residual_risks: The 'illustrative' component of the weight label is a corpus classification not independently tested under Lens A.
